Class EfsFileConnection.Retrieval<E extends IEfsEvent>

java.lang.Object
org.efs.io.EfsFileConnection.Retrieval<E>
Type Parameters:
E - the event type retrieved (must implement IEfsEvent)
All Implemented Interfaces:
AutoCloseable
Enclosing class:
EfsFileConnection<E extends IEfsEvent>
public static final class EfsFileConnection.Retrieval<E extends IEfsEvent> extends Object implements AutoCloseable
Represents an active or completed event retrieval subscription from an EfsFileConnection.

A Retrieval encapsulates a single agent's subscription to events within a specified EfsInterval and matching a CQEngine Query. It manages the delivery of matching historical events and/or future events, along with completion notification.

Instances are created internally by EfsFileConnection.retrieve(org.efs.io.EfsInterval, com.googlecode.cqengine.query.Query<org.efs.io.EfsRow<E>>, java.util.function.Consumer<org.efs.io.EfsRow<E>>, java.util.function.Consumer<org.efs.io.RetrievalCompleteEvent<E>>) and can not be instantiated directly.

Lifecycle

A Retrieval progresses through the following states:

  • Active: Created by retrieve(), the subscription is waiting for or is receiving events. Query isCompleted() to check if still active.
  • Completed: Reached when:
    • All historical events within the interval have been delivered and the interval does not extend into the future.
    • Current time moves past the interval's ending point.
    • Retrieval is cancelled by the caller via close().
    • Underlying EfsFileConnection is closed.
    • Underlying EfsFile is closed.
  • Completion notification: Upon transition to completed, the completion callback provided to retrieve() is invoked exactly once on the agent's dispatcher thread with a RetrievalCompleteEvent specifying completion time and type (e.g., RetrievalCompleteEvent.CompletionType.RETRIEVAL_COMPLETED, RetrievalCompleteEvent.CompletionType.USER_CANCEL, RetrievalCompleteEvent.CompletionType.FILE_CLOSED, or RetrievalCompleteEvent.CompletionType.CONNECTION_CLOSED).

Event Delivery

Matching events are delivered in ascending row-index order via the event callback provided to EfsFileConnection.retrieve(org.efs.io.EfsInterval, com.googlecode.cqengine.query.Query<org.efs.io.EfsRow<E>>, java.util.function.Consumer<org.efs.io.EfsRow<E>>, java.util.function.Consumer<org.efs.io.RetrievalCompleteEvent<E>>). All delivery occurs asynchronously on the agent's dispatcher thread, not on the caller's thread. The callback receives EfsRow instances; access the stored event via EfsRow.getEvent(), the publish timestamp via EfsRow.getPublishTimestamp(), and the row index via EfsRow.getRowIndex().

Cancellation

Call close() to cancel an active retrieval. The method implements AutoCloseable, enabling try-with-resources usage: 


 try (Retrieval<MyEvent> sub = connection.retrieve(...)) {
    // Subscription is active
}  // doClose() is automatically called, cancelling the subscription

Cancellation is idempotent: calling doClose() on an already-completed retrieval has no effect. The completion callback is invoked with RetrievalCompleteEvent.CompletionType.USER_CANCEL if cancellation succeeds.

WARNING! Because events are retrieved asynchronously, placing a Retrieval instance within a try-with-resources requires the current thread to block until the retrieval completes (effectively turning the asynchronous retrieval into synchronous). Failure to do this results in the retrieval request being closed before the request is processed by the event file.

Status and Information

  • isCompleted(): Returns true if the retrieval has reached completion (either naturally or via cancellation).
  • completionType(): Returns the RetrievalCompleteEvent.CompletionType if completed; null if still active.
  • id(): Returns a unique JVM-wide retrieval identifier.
  • agent(): Returns the IEfsAgent owning this retrieval.
  • interval(): Returns the EfsInterval specified when the retrieval was created.
  • toString(): Returns a human-readable summary of the retrieval including ID, agent name, interval, and query.

Threading Model

All Retrieval operations are thread-safe. Status queries (isCompleted(), completionType(), etc.) can be called from any thread and return atomic snapshots. Event delivery and cancellation are coordinated by the underlying file's dispatcher thread, ensuring consistent state transitions.

Integration with EfsFile

Active retrievals are registered with the underlying EfsFile in order to receive matching new rows as they are added (if the interval extends into the future). The file invokes package-private methods (matches(EfsRow), isAtEnd(EfsRow), postRow(EfsEnvelope, Metrics), doClose(Instant, CompletionType)) to match incoming events and notify the retrieval of completion.

Example: Historical Retrieval with Cancellation


 // Retrieve trades from the last 30 minutes
EfsInterval interval = EfsInterval.builder()
    .beginning(EfsDurationEndpoint.builder()
        .timeOffset(Duration.ofMinutes(-30), Clusivity.INCLUSIVE)
        .build())
    .ending(EfsDurationEndpoint.builder()
        .now(Clusivity.INCLUSIVE)
        .build())
    .build();

Query<EfsRow<TradeEvent>> query = QueryFactory.all(TradeEvent.class);

Retrieval<TradeEvent> retrieval = connection.retrieve(
    interval,
    query,
    row -> {
        System.out.println("Trade: " + row.getEvent().symbol()
            + " at row " + row.getRowIndex());
    },
    completion -> {
        System.out.println("Retrieval complete: " + completion.completionType());
    }
);

// Check status
if (!retrieval.isCompleted()) {
    System.out.println("Retrieval " + retrieval.id() + " is active");
}

// Later, cancel if still active
if (!retrieval.isCompleted()) {
    retrieval.doClose();
}

Example: Future Subscription


 // Subscribe to all future trades
EfsInterval interval = EfsInterval.builder()
    .beginning(EfsDurationEndpoint.builder()
        .now(Clusivity.INCLUSIVE)
        .build())
    .ending(EfsDurationEndpoint.builder()
        .endNever()  // No end time
        .build())
    .build();

// Filter for high-value trades
Query<EfsRow<TradeEvent>> query = QueryFactory.greaterThan(
    file.attribute("quantity"), 5000L);

try (Retrieval<TradeEvent> subscription = connection.retrieve(
    interval,
    query,
    row -> System.out.println("Large trade: " + row.getEvent()),
    completion -> System.out.println("Subscription ended")
)) {
    // Subscription is active and will receive all matching future trades
    Thread.sleep(60_000);  // Run for 1 minute
}  // doClose() is automatically called

Error Handling

  • Exceptions thrown by the event callback are logged but do not interrupt the retrieval or prevent other events from being delivered.
  • Exceptions thrown by the completion callback are logged but do not prevent the retrieval from transitioning to completed.
  • If close() is called on an already-completed retrieval, it simply returns without error (idempotent).

Package-Private Implementation Details

The following package-private methods are invoked by EfsFile on the dispatcher thread and should not be called directly:

  • matches(EfsRow): Evaluates whether a newly inserted row satisfies both the interval and user query.
  • isAtEnd(EfsRow): Checks if a row has moved past the interval's ending point.
  • postRow(EfsEnvelope, Metrics): Dispatches a matching row to the event callback on the agent's thread, updating the efs event file metrics as a side effect.
  • doClose(Instant, CompletionType): Marks retrieval as completed (if not already) and invokes completion callback.
  • intervalQuery(Query, Query): Combines beginning, ending, and user queries into a final composite query used for event matching.
